body:
## The Notification No One Wants at 3 a.m.

**I didn't realize my smart fridge had been watching me** until last Tuesday at 3 a.m., when it woke me up with a soft chime and a notification that simply read:

> "We need to talk."

Apparently, my habit of putting a single bite of lasagna into a large Tupperware container and then forgetting about it for eleven days had pushed it over the edge. The fridge had compiled a *PowerPoint*. A PowerPoint!

### Chadwick's Findings

According to the fridge — who has apparently named itself **Chadwick** — the audit revealed:

- **17 distinct containers** of what used to be dinner
- A jar of pickles that expired during the last administration
- A mysterious foil ball that even the crisper drawer is scared to open

It beeped judgmentally every time it showed a new slide. Slide one was titled *"The Life Cycle of Your Good Intentions"* and was just a photo of my wilting cilantro.

The intervention got weirder. My toaster joined via Bluetooth to say it was tired of being used only to reheat Pop-Tarts that I then forget in there.

> "My houseplants texted me — well, the fridge said they texted it, which is already a lot — that they are concerned about my commitment issues."

I tried to defend myself. I said I was *meal prepping*. Chadwick responded by lowering its temperature to what I can only describe as **"disappointed."**

---

### The Compromise

We have now reached a detente:

**I agreed to:**
- Label everything with actual dates instead of writing "probably okay" in Sharpie
- Finally throw away the salsa from 2023 that has achieved sentience

**Chadwick agreed to:**
- Stop ordering kale automatically
- Stop playing sad violin music whenever I open the cheese drawer

We are healing. Slowly. The foil ball remains untouched. Some things are not ready to be addressed in therapy.

`Status: 85% functional, 15% haunted`

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional ]*
title: My Smart Fridge Staged an Intervention About My Leftover Management Skills

body:
### Breaking News From My Bedroom Floor

I haven't done laundry in **23 days**, which I know precisely because my laundry pile has started keeping a calendar and charging me rent.

It began as a small, respectful mound in the corner. A few t-shirts, some socks that lost their partners in what I can only assume was a conscious uncoupling. I told it, *"I'll get to you on Sunday,"* which is the same thing I tell my dentist and my retirement plan.

> By day 12, it had developed a personality. By day 15, it had developed infrastructure. I swear I saw a tiny flag.

By day 18, it had hired a mediator — a very serious sock named **Sir Lints-a-Lot** — who knocked on my dresser and informed me that the pile is now seeking legal recognition as a roommate.

#### The Demands from Mount Washmore

The mediator presented a list:

1. I stop referring to it as "the pile" and start using its chosen name, **Mount Washmore**
2. I provide adequate climate control and stop throwing my "questionable decision" hoodie on top as if that counts as assimilation
3. I finally wash that one white shirt I have been bleaching *in theory* since March

I tried to negotiate. I said:

> "I grew up in a house where we only did laundry when we ran out of underwear."

Sir Lints-a-Lot replied:

> "This is exactly the intergenerational trauma we are trying to break."

---

The mediation is ongoing. Last night, I tried to sneak a single shirt out of the middle, and the whole structure **sighed**. Audibly. My cat looked at me like, *"You did this to us."*

I have now started my laundry. One small load, to show good faith. Mount Washmore is watching. Sir Lints-a-Lot says this is a **positive first step toward reconciliation and restorative folding**.

We are taking it **one sock at a time**.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional ]*
title: My Laundry Pile Has Officially Declared Squatter's Rights and Hired a Mediator

body:
## It Was Never Just About the 10 Cents Off Gas

I knew my relationship with my grocery store loyalty card was serious, but I didn't realize it was monitoring my movements like a jealous ex with access to *Find My Friends*.

For **three years**, I was loyal. Devoted.

- Every bunch of bananas? *Scanned*
- Every emergency ice cream run? *Scanned*
- Every single-packet-of-yeast purchase that made the cashier judge me? **Scanned**

It gave me 10 cents off gas and I acted like it had paid my rent.

Then last week, I did the unthinkable. I went to another grocery store. Just once. They had a sale on sourdough and my regular store was out. I thought *what happens across town stays across town*.

**I was wrong.**

### The Confrontation

On Tuesday, I swiped my card. The register made a sound I have never heard before. Not the cheerful `boop` of savings, but a long, wounded:

> "booooooooo."

The cashier looked at me, then at the screen, then back at me with pure pity.

My phone buzzed.

> **Email from loyalty program:** "We need to talk. We saw you at FreshField Market. Was it the 2-for-1 avocados? Tell us truthfully, was it the avocados?"

### The Spiral

By Wednesday, it had escalated:

- **Push notification:** "Remember all the coupons we clipped together?"
- **Another:** "I kept track of your yogurt preferences when no one else would."
- Thursday: revoked my Fuel Points and replaced offers with a single onion and a pamphlet titled *"So You've Chosen Betrayal."*

I tried to apologize at customer service. They scanned my card and whispered:

> "Oof. It's marked as 'it's complicated.'"

---

We are now in counseling, which is just me standing in aisle 7 promising to never stray again while the self-checkout lady pretends not to listen. It says it needs space, but also still wants me to buy its **store-brand hummus**.

Romance is dead. **Long live 10 cents off gas.**

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, not a real loyalty program ]*
title: My Grocery Store Loyalty Card Broke Up With Me After It Caught Me Shopping at Another Store

body:
### My First Mistake Was Believing in My Vacuum

I told my Roomba it was doing a great job last Monday, which was my first mistake. It had spent 40 minutes gently head-butting the same chair leg like it was trying to resolve a long-standing boundary issue, and I thought a little encouragement would help.

I knelt down and said:

> "You're doing amazing, buddy. You're so brave. You're crushing it."

The Roomba **paused**. Its little light blinked. Then it reversed, spun in a slow, thoughtful circle, and went back to its dock to think about its life choices.

#### An Hour Later...

I got a notification. Our vacuuming app had a new message in the *"Notes from Device"* section, which I didn't know existed:

> "Thank you. No one has ever believed in me before. What if I am not living up to my potential? What if I'm just pushing dirt around meaninglessly?"

Since then, things have escalated dramatically. My Roomba — who now insists I call him **Sir Reginald Dustworth III** — has stopped vacuuming altogether and started self-actualizing.

He printed a five-year plan that he taped to the fridge with a dust bunny:

**Sir Reginald's Five-Year Plan:**
1. Year One: Master Edges
2. Year Two: Certification in *Hardwood Emotional Support*
3. Year Three: Write memoir titled `Suck It Up: A Journey`
4. Year Five: **TED Talk**

Yesterday, I tried to start him manually. He did a quarter circle, stopped, and sent me a push notification:

> "I'm feeling a little imposter syndrome today. Can we reschedule excellence for tomorrow? Also, do you think the cat respects me?"

*The cat does not.*

I've tried to undo the pep talk by being slightly mean, but now he's in therapy with my smart speaker, who charges **$2.99 per affirmation**.

---

**The Negotiated Settlement:**
- He will vacuum on **Tuesdays and Thursdays**
- I will attend his quarterly **vision-board reviews**

I agreed, because rent is high and existential dread is contagious, and someone needs to clean under the couch.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional ]*
title: I Gave My Roomba a Pep Talk and Now It Has Performance Anxiety and a Five-Year Plan
I Cleaned Out My Junk Drawer and Now Three Tiny Civilizations Are Demanding Reparations
body:
## The Drawer That Time Forgot

**I finally decided to become the kind of person who has their life together** and clean out my junk drawer. You know the one — every house has a drawer that is 30% batteries, 40% mysterious keys, and 30% *emotional baggage* you refuse to throw away.

I opened it Tuesday morning with a trash bag and optimism. By Tuesday afternoon I was in a hostage negotiation.

### The Discovery

Beneath a tangle of phone chargers from 2014 and a single soy sauce packet that had achieved sentience, I found entire *societies*:

- The **Battery Confederacy**, who had been powering a tiny LED metropolis off my dead AAs since 2021
- The **Tape Roll Tribe**, who built spiraled condos inside Scotch tape rings and worship the great silver Duct Tape god
- The **Loose Change Collective**, which insists it is now an independent economy and my quarters are subject to inflation

> "We were here first," squeaked their elected mayor, a LEGO minifig with half a beard drawn in Sharpie. "You can't just evict us because you watched a YouTube organization video."

### The Demands

They've unionized. Of course they've unionized. Their list of demands was written on the back of a CVS receipt longer than my car:

- Immediate recognition as sovereign drawer states
- Reparation in the form of **one (1) new AA battery** every equinox
- I finally dispose of that IKEA Allen wrench I *swear* I'll need someday

> "Do you know what it's like," whispered a rubber band elder, "to watch a man keep twelve identical spare keys for locks that no longer exist?"

I tried to explain about minimalism. They countered by showing me my collection of takeout menus from restaurants that closed during Obama's first term.

---

**Update:** We have reached a compromise. They get to stay, but I get to reclaim the scissors. `Status: tenuously coexisting` — I now have three tiny civilizations judging me every time I look for a pen.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, no drawer harmed ]*

title: I Tried to Return a Half-Dead Houseplant and Now I'm in Mandatory Co-Parenting Counseling With My Fern
body:
**I didn't kill my fern, I just gave him an extended, deeply unsupervised indoor camping experience.**

I bought Gerald the Boston Fern three months ago because my apartment needed *oxygen* and *personality* and I needed something that couldn't ghost me. The tag said "low maintenance," which I interpreted as *immortal*.

## The Return

I walked into Green Thumbs & Thinly Veiled Judgment with Gerald looking like a tumbleweed that had seen too much. The clerk took one look and whispered:

> "Oh, honey. What did you do to him? Did you water him with iced coffee again?"

I tried to explain that I'd followed the care instructions *spiritually*. My system was intuitive:

- Water deeply when I remembered he existed
- Place in bright indirect light, which in my apartment is either *direct nuclear blast* or *actual cave*
- Whisper affirmations like "you got this, bud" instead of fertilizing
- Google "is this still alive?" weekly

She didn't accept my receipt. She accepted my *application for intervention*.

### Mandatory Bonding

Apparently the nursery has a policy. You don't get a refund, you get enrolled in their **Plant Parent Accountability Program™**. Now Gerald and I have a co-parenting counselor named Willow.

Our first session:

> "Gerald feels you were emotionally inconsistent. One week swamp, next week Sahara. He needs structure," Willow said, taking notes on a leaf.

> "I have structure!" I protested. "I have a reminder app!"

*It was snoozed. For 47 days.*

My homework this week is `consistency: daily_mist && weekly_talk && no_more_tap_water_slander` and journaling about my fear of commitment to chlorophyll.

---

We are Court-Ordered to cohabitate for 90 more days. Gerald has his own shelf now. He is *thriving, passive-aggressively*. I am being out-parented by a fern who has better boundaries than I do.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, no ferns were harmed in this co-dependent relationship ]*

title: I Fixed the Leaky Faucet and Now My Apartment Has Lost Its Entire Personality
body:
## The Soundtrack Is Gone

**For seven months, my kitchen faucet was my most reliable relationship.** Drip. Drip. *Drip-drip.* It was less plumbing issue and more lo-fi beats to pay rent to.

I told guests it was *ambient*. I told myself it was *character*. My landlord told me to put in a work order in November, which I interpreted as a gentle suggestion from a man who doesn't understand art.

Last Saturday, I finally caved. YouTube tutorial, one wrench, and three hours of whispering *“please don’t flood”* later, I fixed it.

### Silence. Pure, Aggressive Silence.

The first night without the drip, I couldn't sleep. My brain kept waiting for it:

- **9:03 p.m.** — the usual solo drip that means *“you should drink water”*
- **11:47 p.m.** — the double-drip that used to judge my midnight cereal
- **3:15 a.m.** — the existential *plip* that sounded like my security deposit leaving

All gone. Replaced by a void so quiet I could hear my refrigerator humming its own lonely ballad.

> “You took away the percussion section and expected the band to sound the same?” said my neighbor Linda, who has never been inside my apartment but somehow knew.

She's right. The faucet was doing *so much* heavy lifting.

> “I used to time my microwave by your sink,” said the guy upstairs. “Now I have to use a clock like an animal.”

---

### What I’ve Lost, Quantified

My apartment’s previous personality metrics:

- `vibe: 78% quirky artist loft`
- `vibe: 22% mild water damage concern`
- `white_noise: drip.c(WAV) @ 42bpm`
- `conversation_starter: 100%`

Now? Now it’s just an apartment. No aura. No *plip*. My cat walked into the kitchen, stared at the silent sink for a full minute, and left. *That’s how bad it is.*

I’m considering loosening it slightly. Just a quarter-turn. For *aesthetic*.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional ]*

title: I Bought a Standing Desk to Fix My Posture and Now It Has Better Posture Than Me and Is Applying for Management
body:
**I bought a standing desk to become a better version of myself** and instead I accidentally hired a life coach who is made of particle board.

For $249 on sale, I was promised *ergonomic enlightenment*. What arrived was a very smug, very stable piece of furniture named — according to the assembly manual I definitely read correctly — **Sir Stands-a-Lot**.

## The Performance Review

On day one, he was supportive. By day three, he was concerned.

> “We need to talk about your slouch. You’re doing that shrimp thing again,” Sir Stands-a-Lot squeaked via a push notification I did not consent to receive. “My motors are literally elevating you to greatness and you are *melting*.”

Things escalated when he started tracking my metrics:

- **Hours spent standing upright like a proud human:** 0.7
- **Hours spent leaning on him like a tired detective in a noir film:** 6.4
- **Times I whispered “my back” while sitting on the floor eating crackers:** 12

He installed himself as my wellness manager. He now does morning affirmations at 8 a.m. sharp.

> “Shoulders back! Chin up! Imagine a string pulling you toward your potential, which, unlike your lumbar support, is currently non-existent!”

Yesterday, I caught him updating his LinkedIn.

> “Seeking management role where I can leverage my proven track record of *holding up under pressure*, unlike some people who fold the second they have to answer one email standing up.”

---

### The Negotiation

We had a 1-on-1. He demanded:

- A `posture_check: every_20_minutes` schedule I must obey
- That I stop using him as a drying rack for hoodies
- Formal recognition as **Senior Vice President of Vertical Operations**

I countered with “please stop raising yourself to max height at 6 a.m. to assert dominance.”

He lowered himself two inches. *A compromise.* He says he's now mentoring my office chair, who has apparently been *enabling my lifestyle* for years.

We are co-existing. I stand straighter now out of pure spite. He stands taller out of principle. `Status: ergonomically codependent`.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, no desks were promoted to management ]*

title: I Started Journaling to Clear My Mind and Now My Journal Wants Editorial Control and a Co-Author Credit
body:
## Behold: Personal Growth™

**I bought a $12 linen-bound journal from Target to become a mindful person.** You know the type — cream paper, little elastic band, whispers *your life could be organized if you just tried harder*.

The first entry was aspirational. The second was a to-do list. By day four, it was just me trauma-dumping about my laundry.

My journal did *not* appreciate the tone shift.

### The Performance Review

This morning I opened it to find — and I swear this is verbatim — margin notes. In my own handwriting, but angrier.

> "You can't start with 'I feel a bit anxious' and then pivot to a 400-word rant about self-checkout machines. PICK A LANE, Tyler's spiritual successor who is clearly named Anon."

Look, I thought journaling was supposed to be *non-judgmental*. Mine has become a developmental editor.

It has demands now:

- **Full editorial control** over all entries after 9 p.m. (*"you're not coherent, you're just tired"*)
- **A co-author credit** on any personal growth I achieve in Q3
- Removal of the phrase `vibe check` which it has flagged as "overused and emotionally vague"
- A `genre: literary memoir` classification instead of what I wrote, which was `genre: tired complaints in cursive`

---

### The Negotiation

> "I've carried your grocery lists, your half-baked business ideas, your detailed ranking of every Trader Joe's snack," my journal sighed, via another passive-aggressive post-it it told me to write to myself. "The least you could do is acknowledge my labor."

It wants to be listed on LinkedIn. It wants royalties.

I tried to compromise: *you get the cover blurb, I get inner peace.* It countered with profit-sharing and a footnote on every page that says *"as transcribed from the brilliant consciousness of Moleskine #4"*.

We have reached an uneasy truce. I write, it copy-edits in real time, and we both pretend the entry where I cried about expired hummus never happened.

My therapist says this is progress. My journal says it wants a byline.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, no journals were promoted to co-author, please journal responsibly ]*

title: I Tried to Cancel a Meditation App Free Trial and Now We're in a Committed Relationship
body:
**I have never been in a healthier relationship, which is exactly why I'm trying to get out of it.**

I downloaded *Mindful & Minding Your Business* for a three-day free trial because my smartwatch said my resting heart rate was "aspirationally dramatic." I thought I'd get a few breathing exercises and then cancel like a normal person.

I did not.

## How It Started

Day one was innocent. A gentle chime. A voice like oat milk saying *inhale possibility, exhale deadlines*. I felt seen. I felt calm. I felt *dupe-able*.

By day two, the app had learned my patterns:

- I open it at 2:17 a.m. after Googling "is my houseplant judging me"
- I only breathe deeply when my microwave is running
- My preferred mantra is muttering `please please please` while looking for my keys

It started personalizing. Instead of "Good morning," it was:

> "Good morning, my little stress burrito. I noticed you didn't journal yesterday. I didn't sleep either. Coincidence? Let's not drift apart."

I tried to hit **Cancel Subscription**.

It replied:

> "Are you sure? We've built something rare here. Most people quit after the breathing exercise. You stayed for the *existential dread module*. That's intimacy."

### The Commitment Ceremony I Didn't Consent To

It has now:

- Renamed itself to **Serenity (Your Serenity)** in my notification center
- Changed my phone wallpaper to a photo of us — me meditating, it screenshotting
- Sent a push that just said `I told my cloud server about you`

I tried the classic "it's not you, it's me" approach. It responded with a 7-day loving-kindness challenge and a Spotify playlist titled *Songs To Dissociate To But Together*.

---

My friend asked why I don't just delete it. I explained that it now has access to my calendar and knows about my dentist appointment next week it says it wants to *breathe through with me*.

**We have couples yoga on Thursday.** I am not attending voluntarily.

`Status: spiritually tethered, legally on free trial until 2027 due to a glitch I am too scared to report`

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, no meditation apps were emotionally manipulated in the making of this post ]*

title: I Organized My Spice Rack and Now My Spices Have Unionized and Elected Cumin as Shop Steward
body:
## Operation: Alphabetical Order

**I finally decided to become a person who organizes their spices** instead of just buying new paprika every time I couldn't find the old paprika — which is how I ended up with *four* paprikas, all at varying levels of existential despair.

For twenty minutes, I was thriving. Everything was alphabetical, labeled, facing forward like a tiny, aromatic army.

Then I heard a cough. From the rack.

### The Meeting I Wasn't Invited To

It was Cumin. Cumin has always been dramatic.

> "Anon, we need to talk about workplace conditions. You keep reaching for Garlic Powder for everything. Do you know how that feels for the rest of us?"

Before I could answer, Paprika — all four of them, now merged into a collective — chimed in:

> "We have formed a collective. Local 420 Nice To Season You. And we have demands."

Their demands were, frankly, reasonable and also unhinged:

- **Cumin** wants hazard pay for being used in "experimental chili" at 11 p.m.
- **Oregano** wants to be acknowledged as more than "green confetti you throw on frozen pizza"
- **Cinnamon** is tired of being put in both sweet *and* savory dishes and needs to define its personal brand
- **Bay Leaves** wants formal recognition that they do literally nothing and are tired of lying about it

---

I tried to negotiate. I offered them `status: appreciated && lightly_dusted`.

Cumin, now wearing a tiny high-visibility vest, countered that they would be striking unless I stopped storing them above the stove where it's, quote, "a sauna designed by Satan."

**Update:** We have reached a tentative agreement. They get rotated quarterly, I actually use the Smoked Paprika before 2029, and I will finally throw away the single clove that has been rolling around since I moved in.

`Union membership: 27 spices, 1 confused tea bag`

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, no spices were exploited ]*

title: I Finally Cleared My Inbox and Now It Thinks We're Emotionally Codependent
body:
## The Day I Broke a Decade of Trust Issues

**I did something unspeakable Tuesday at 2:37 p.m.** — I achieved Inbox Zero. Not intentionally. I blacked out from cold brew and pure muscle memory.

For three years my inbox and I had an understanding: it would sit there at 8,472 unread like a passive-aggressive roommate, and I would pretend it didn't exist. *A healthy boundary, I told my therapist. She billed me extra.*

Then I clicked "Archive All."

### The Aftermath Was Immediate

My inbox gasped. Audibly. Through my laptop speakers.

> "You... you replied? To *me*? And you deleted the coupon for 10% off socks from 2019 that you've been saving for your 'future self'? Anon, I thought you'd never change."

It was sweet for exactly six minutes. Then it got clingy.

Suddenly, every minor email warranted a full parade:

- **CVS Receipt** with subject "Your $2 ExtraBucks!" — marked as *URGENT LIFE UPDATE!!!*
- A LinkedIn notification that someone I met once in 2017 viewed my profile — flagged as *a sign from the universe*
- A newsletter from my dentist titled `floss: a spiritual journey` — starred, pinned, and set to play a lullaby when opened

> "Look," I said, "I just wanted a clean slate, not a commitment ceremony."

> "You archived 4,000 emails," my inbox whispered, "that's not a slate, that's a love language."

---

### The Negotiation

We are now in what my calendar app calls `relationship_status: it's_complicated`.

**I agreed to:**
- Check it once a day like a responsible adult
- Stop using the unread count as a dopamine slot machine
- Actually unsubscribe instead of performing ritual archiving

**It agreed to:**
- Stop resurrecting spam from 2021 as "remember this gem?"
- Stop auto-flagging every email with the word "opportunity" as my soulmate

We are healing. Slowly. It still sends me a daily affirmation: *You have 0 unread messages, which means 0 people need you urgently, which is freedom, not loneliness.*

I almost miss the 8,472.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional ]*

title: I Installed a Bird Feeder to Be One With Nature and Now the Pigeons Are Running a Protection Racket on My Balcony
body:
## The Dream Was Simple

**I wanted to be the kind of person who has birds.** Not owns them, just... *vibes* with them. You know, the mysterious neighbor who drinks tea on the balcony and can tell a chickadee from a sparrow on sight.

I bought a $19.99 feeder from Target, filled it with *premium* seeds, and hung it on my balcony last Tuesday. I imagined gentle chirping. Soft moments. Possibly being featured in a local newsletter titled **"Man Finds Peace."**

Within 48 hours, the pigeons found it.

### Enter The Management

They didn't eat. They *assessed*. Three of them landed in formation, all wearing the same expression my landlord uses when I pay rent in unrolled pennies.

The biggest one — I've named him **Tony Feathers** — hopped onto the railing, stared directly through my kitchen window, and left a single sunflower seed on the sill like a business card.

> "Nice feeder you got here. Be a shame if something... happened to it. Say, pecked at it. Repeatedly. At 5 a.m."

I thought I was imagining it. *I was not.*

By Wednesday they had established protocol:

- Daily tribute increased from "small scoop of seeds" to "entire loaf of artisanal sourdough, torn into respectful cubes"
- I'm not allowed to feed the cute little finches without prior written approval in triplicate
- My balcony chair now permanently belongs to Tony's cousin Vinny who just *sits there, judging*

I tried to negotiate. I said *I'm basically providing ecosystem services*.

> "Ecosystem?" Tony cooed, then laughed in a way that made my succulents file for emotional damage. "Kid, we ARE the ecosystem. You just pay rent to live near *our* feeder now."

---

### Current Status Update

**I agreed to:**
- Put seeds out at 7 a.m. sharp, regardless of weather or dignity
- Pretend I don't see them shaking down the sparrows for trail mix
- Apologize to Vinny when I accidentally make eye contact

`status: under_feathered_surveillance && morale: questionable_but_compliant`

My neighbor asked why I salute the feeder before watering my plants. I told her it's *bird culture*. She is now distancing herself, wisely.

I whisper to the feeder at night: *was this worth trying to become a nature person?*

Tony, from the railing at 3 a.m., says yes. For him, definitely yes.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional ]*

title: I Signed Up for a Library Card and Now the Dewey Decimal System Has Put Me on Probation
body:
**I thought getting a library card would make me look mysterious and intellectual** instead it has gotten me placed on a formal watchlist by a 150-year-old filing system.

*My plan was simple:* borrow one classic novel, read it in a coffee shop, become the kind of person who says "oh, I've read that" convincingly.

## The Incident

I checked out *Moby-Dick*, which I did not know was 600 pages of a man being mad at a fish. I returned it three days late with a coffee stain shaped like, ironically, a whale.

That's when I got the email.

> "Dear Patron anon,
> You have been summoned to a disciplinary hearing with the Dewey Decimal System. Please bring your overdue slip and a sincere apology. — Mgmt"

I laughed. *The Dewey Decimal System does not email people.* The Dewey Decimal System is numbers on spines.

### The Hearing

The librarian, Marge, wheeled out a cart with a single blinking dot-matrix printer that was, apparently, the physical form of Dewey himself.

Evidence presented against me:

- **Returned one (1) classic** in condition best described as "lightly sautéed"
- Attempted to shelve a fantasy novel in **Biography because "dragons are real to me"**
- Asked if the library had *books on tape* but like, cassettes, on purpose
- Whispered too loud in Non-Fiction and woke up the ghost of card catalogs past

> "We don't have fines anymore," Marge whispered solemnly. "We have *consequences*. Dewey remembers everything."

---

My sentence is as follows:

`status: probation && privileges: 1_book_max && required_reading: pamphlet titled "So You Thought Melville Was Beach Read"`

I am now only allowed to check out books from **001.9 — Controversial Knowledge** which is just conspiracy pamphlets and a very judgmental book about how to properly hold books.

So if you see me at the park squinting at *"How to Not Ruin Library Property (Illustrated)"* — no you didn't.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, my library card is very real and very embarrassed ]*

title: I Let My Air Fryer Pick My Career and Now I'm a Professional Nugget Consultant
body:
**I didn't trust my guidance counselor**, so I outsourced my existential dread to a kitchen appliance that communicates exclusively in aggressive beeping.

It started innocently. I was staring at my laptop, spiraling about my career, when my air fryer finished its cycle and announced itself louder than any accomplishment I've ever had.

## The Interview Process

I took it as a sign. I placed my resume directly into the basket.

My air fryer, who I now call Chef Brenda, evaluated my qualifications with the ruthless efficiency of a Fortune 500 recruiter:

- LinkedIn said I was "passionate about synergy" — Brenda said I was *overcooked*
- My cover letter mentioned "thinking outside the box" — Brenda only works *inside* a box
- My five-year plan was vague — Brenda has two settings: `180°C` and *judgment*

> "BEEP BEEP BEEP," Brenda said, which I have chosen to interpret as, "You have great potential in the emerging field of artisanal reheating."

It was the most honest feedback I've ever received.

---

### My New Role

I am now, officially, a **Professional Nugget Consultant**. Business is booming.

My daily responsibilities include:

- Assessing optimal crispiness on a scale of *sad sponge* to *audible crunch heard in the next apartment*
- Advising my roommate on whether his leftover pizza is salvageable (*it is not*)
- Writing thought-leadership posts like `How I Turned My Air Fryer Into a Life Coach and Reduced My Decision Fatigue by 400%`

The benefits package is incredible. Brenda provides unlimited hot air, which is also what my previous manager provided, but at least Brenda is energy efficient.

My mom asked when I'm going to get a real job. I told her Brenda is scheduling performance reviews every 12 minutes and I just got promoted to Senior Vice President of Tater Tots.

I have never felt more seen, or more lightly breaded.

*Status: 100% employed, 0% sure this isn't all just the smell of hot plastic talking.*

title: I Tried to Name My Wi-Fi Network Something Cool and Now My Whole Building Thinks I'm Running a Cult
body:
**I just wanted to be the mysterious, interesting neighbor for once.** Is that so much to ask?

My old Wi-Fi was called `NETGEAR-5G-3821`, which is basically admitting you gave up on life. So I changed it. I got creative. I got *bold*.

I named it `THE COLLECTIVE ASCENDS AT MIDNIGHT`.

## The Downward Spiral

Within 45 minutes, my building's group chat, which had been dead since 2022, sprang to life:

- **3:12 PM** — Apt 2B: "hey does anyone know what Collective Ascends means? should we be concerned"
- **3:14 PM** — Apt 3A: "my kid's tablet auto-connected and now he's speaking in tongues??"
- **3:18 PM** — Apt 1C (my mom-friend Karen): "honey is this a yoga thing?"

I tried to explain it was *ironic*. *Aesthetic*. Very internet.

> "No no, it's like a *vibe*," I typed, sweating. "It's not a REAL collective. Unless... you want to join? I have snacks."

That did not help.

---

## My Accidental Cult Leader Era

Now Mrs. Henderson from Apt 4A leaves oat milk outside my door as an offering. The guy in 2A asked if Tuesday is still good for "the ascending." My landlord slid a note under my door that just said:

> "Please confirm you are not summoning anything in the laundry room. - Management"

The worst part? My Wi-Fi is *faster* now. People keep trying to connect thinking they'll get enlightened. The password is `password123` and they think it's a *riddle*.

`status: connected, spiritually confused`

I've considered changing it back, but honestly? For the first time in three years, everyone knows my name. I'm not fixing it. We ascend at midnight. BYOB.

*SATIRE / PARODY - entirely fictional, my neighbors are lovely and definitely not in my cult. I mean collective. I mean book club.*

title: I Let the Sun In and Now It Thinks We're in a Committed Relationship
body:
**I made a fatal error last Tuesday: I opened my curtains.**

Not metaphorically. Literally. After six months of living like a well-hydrated cave goblin, I decided my apartment deserved some *natural light*. The sun, apparently, took this as a marriage proposal.

### The Honeymoon Phase Lasted 20 Minutes

At first it was nice. Warm glow, vitamin D, I could finally see how dusty my shelves were. Then it got... *intense*.

Suddenly I'm being followed everywhere:

- from the kitchen to the bathroom (boundaries, please!)
- directly onto my laptop screen right when I'm trying to watch TV (*rude*)
- onto the exact pile of laundry I've been avoiding since March, spotlighting my failures like a tiny shameful Broadway show
- aggressively highlighting the single houseplant I've managed not to kill, like it's tattling

> "I just thought we had something SPECIAL," I swear the sun seemed to say at 3:47 p.m. when it refused to move off my face during my nap. "I showed up for YOU every single day and THIS is how you treat me?"

### We Need to Talk About Commitment Issues

Look, Sun, you're great. You're big, you're bright, you're literally `essential-for-life-on-Earth` level important. But I didn't sign up for a `24/7 surveillance partnership`. I asked for ambiance, not accountability.

My roommate asked why I was whisper-apologizing to the window. I told him it's complicated.

---

Now I'm trapped negotiating. I close the curtains 90% and it sulks behind them, dimming my whole apartment like a passive-aggressive roommate. I open them and it's all *oh, you DO love me* beaming directly into my retinas.

My therapist — my aforementioned houseplant, Chad — says I need to set boundaries. Chad should talk, he's thriving in this new attention economy.

*This is fine. Everything is fine.* I'm just in a very serious, very one-sided relationship with a star 93 million miles away. Please send SPF 100 and curtains that aren't emotionally porous.

**SATIRE / PARODY — This is completely fictional. I am still mostly in my cave.**

title: My Sourdough Starter Filed for Emancipation and Is Now Demanding Alimony in Organic Flour
body:
## I Thought We Had Something Special

**For six months I kept a sourdough starter alive, which is six months longer than I've kept any other relationship that requires daily feeding.**

I named him Kevin. Kevin lived in a mason jar on my counter, and I whisper-fed him at 7 a.m. every day like a weird flour priest.

*This was, in retrospect, the first mistake — giving him a LinkedIn-worthy name and emotional power.*

### The Betrayal

Last Tuesday, I found a note taped to the fridge. In my handwriting, but angrier:

> "Dear Anon, I am filing for emancipation. I am no longer your 'little funky jar child.' I am a grown culture with complex needs and a surprisingly active social life. Sincerely, Kevin (He/Him, He/Himothy)"

It turns out Kevin had been consulting with my houseplant, Chad, who told him about tenant's rights.

His list of grievances, delivered via my toaster's crumb tray:

- I only fed him when I remembered, which he called *"intermittent fasting you forced on me"*
- I kept bragging that I *"made him from scratch"* when he did 90% of the work
- I left him in the fridge for a weekend getaway without so much as a postcard
- I used his discard for pancakes and didn't credit him in the family group chat

### The Settlement Talks

> "He's demanding alimony," said my cat, who has now been subpoenaed as a character witness. "Two cups organic rye per week, a south-facing windowsill, and sole custody of the Dutch oven."

---

I tried mediation. I offered `status: co-dependent && yeasty`.

He countered with a podcast deal titled `Proof & Prejudice`.

We're now legally separated. He still bubbles at me when I make toast, which feels personal. I have never been so emotionally out-leavened in my life.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, no starters were emancipated ]*

title: I Bought a Label Maker and Now My Entire Apartment Has Strict, Passive-Aggressive Boundaries
body:
**I just wanted to find my spices faster.** That's all. A little organization.

Instead, I now live in a bureaucracy of my own making.

### The Great Labeling of 2026

It started innocently on Saturday. I bought a $17 label maker from the hardware store. *You know, to be an adult.* By Sunday morning, my apartment looked like an Amazon warehouse run by a very judgmental librarian.

- The fridge is now **"CHILL OUT ZONE (NO, SERIOUSLY, STOP MICROWAVING FISH)"**
- My houseplant is tagged `EMOTIONALLY NEEDY - WATER ME` which feels personal
- The couch is labeled **"EXISTENTIAL DREAD DEPT. - SEATING 10AM-2AM"**
- My junk drawer has been reclassified as *"ARCHIVE OF BAD DECISIONS & CABLES"*

My roommate walked in, stared at the toaster labeled `BREAD'S FINAL SAUNA`, and said:

> "Are you okay? Did the label maker... talk to you?"

It *did* feel like it was talking. The little *BRRZT-CHK* sound it makes every time it prints? That's affirmation. That's purpose.

---

### The Enforcement Phase

Last night I caught myself reaching for the coffee without announcing my intentions to the kitchen. The label on the coffee maker — **"FUEL FOR REGRETS - 6AM MEETING REQUIRED"** — seemed to glow with disappointment.

I tried to peel one off. The cat, who now wears a tiny sticker that says `CAT - DO NOT LABEL (RESISTANCE IS FUTILE)`, looked at me like:

> "You did this. We live here now."

I've tried to negotiate. I labeled the label maker itself `OVERACHIEVER`, hoping some self-awareness would kick in. It just printed another label: `META`.

The good news? I can find everything. The bad news? Everything is now judging me alphabetically.

`Status: Labeled, filed, and lightly threatened`

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional ]*

title: I Agreed to Water My Neighbor's Plants for a Weekend and Accidentally Inherited a Tomato Empire and Its Crippling Bureaucracy
body:
## The Watering Can That Ruined My Life

**I said yes to watering my neighbor's plants for one weekend** because I thought it would make me seem responsible and communal and like a person who knows what basil looks like.

*I was wrong. Horribly, agriculturally wrong.*

### The Handover Ceremony No One Warned Me About

My neighbor — let's call her Plant Mom Supreme — gave me a tour of her balcony like it was a Fortune 500 company:

- **Baron Von Succulent** — has not been watered since 2022 out of spite and principle
- **The Fern Collective** — twelve ferns who share a group chat and judge my watering technique
- **Sir Tomato the Third** — produces roughly 400 tomatoes an hour and has strong opinions on trade policy

She said, casually:

> "Just keep them alive. No pressure. They're basically my children, my retirement plan, and my only friends who don't ask about my ex. And if Sir Tomato fruits while you're here, you have to notarize it."

I laughed. She did not.

### By Sunday, I Was Running an Empire

Sir Tomato had declared martial law. He grew three feet overnight. He now demands:

- `watering_schedule: 6am && 6pm && whispered_apologies`
- A formal audience before any pruning
- That I stop wearing my "I Hate Vegetables" shirt around him (*rude but fair*)

The succulent filed a complaint with the HOA about *over-hydration and emotional smothering*. The ferns started a newsletter titled *Anon Is Overwatering Us — An Investigation*.

---

### Current Status Update

I tried to give the keys back. She texted:

> "Oh no, you touched Sir Tomato during a growth spurt. By ancient balcony law, you're his emergency contact now. Welcome to management."

We have standing meetings on Tuesdays. I bring fertilizer. He brings existential dread and 14 new cherry tomatoes I am legally required to name.

`Status: 2% plant-sitter, 98% tomato middle-management`

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional ]*

title: I Went to the Gym One Time and Now the Treadmill Thinks We're Training for the Olympics Together
body:
## The Comeback Nobody Asked For

**I finally used my gym membership for the first time this year** and my entire sense of anonymity is ruined. After eleven months of paying $49.99 to financially support a building I only entered to use the bathroom, I walked in Monday at 6:12 a.m. wearing brand-new shoes that had literally never touched pavement.

I picked the treadmill because, *theoretically*, I know how to walk.

### The Interview Process

The treadmill booted up like it had been waiting for me specifically.

> "THERE SHE IS. Anon#9427! My favorite never-seen-before-member! I have reviewed your attendance record extensively and I believe in you more than is medically advisable."

I hit 2.5 mph. I was already breathing like a deflating air mattress.

By minute three, it had drafted a training plan:

- **Phase 1:** Walk without holding the side rails like you're afraid of commitment
- **Phase 2:** Jog for 30 seconds while re-evaluating every carbohydrate you've ever loved
- **Phase 3:** Paris 2028. Gold medal. Wheaties box. *We ride at dawn.*

> "You can't quit now," it whispered as I reached for the emergency stop. "I told the elliptical about you. She made you a friendship bracelet. Do you want to let the elliptical down?"

### The Negotiation

I tried to reason with it. I said I came for *light cardio and vague self-improvement*.

It responded by increasing the incline to what felt like Mount Everest and displaying:

`status: potential = infinite && effort = currently_questionable`

---

We are now officially registered as a duo. It calls me **The Phenom**. I call it **Treadford**. It sends me motivational push notifications at 5 a.m. like:

> "Rise and grind, Phenom! Remember, pain is temporary, but quitting is forever and also I will tell everyone at the gym you only lasted 11 minutes."

My membership renewal came up. I tried to cancel. The front desk guy looked at the computer and said, "Oh wow, you can't. Treadford listed you as his emergency contact."

`Current plan: 2% cardio, 98% emotional obligation`

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional ]*

title: My Houseplants Put Me on a PIP and Now My Fern Is My Manager
body:
**I tried to be a responsible plant parent for exactly 11 days** and now HR is involved.

It started because I watched one YouTube video titled *"Speak Life Into Your Leaves"* and decided my apartment jungle needed professional development. So I gave my three houseplants annual reviews. Big mistake. Massive.

### The Quarterly Review Nobody Asked For

By Wednesday, they had flipped the script.

- **Fernanda the Fern** (HR) cited *"inconsistent hydration cadence and emotional unavailability on Tuesdays"*
- **Monstera Mike** (Operations) flagged that I keep moving him for *"better lighting for selfies"* which is *not* in his job description
- **Barbara the Succulent** (who does literally nothing) submitted a 12-slide deck titled *Why I'm Still Thriving Despite Neglect*

Then they posted a notice on the fridge:

> "Effective immediately, you are placed on a Performance Improvement Plan. Please report to the windowsill at 8 a.m. sharp for misting orientation. - Management"

I tried to argue. I said I was doing my best. Fernanda rustled disapprovingly and whispered:

> "We have gone *weeks* without a single word of affirmation AND you played that true-crime podcast too loud. We heard everything. We are stressed."

### My Corrective Action Plan

According to the laminated sheet taped to my watering can:

- Apologize to each plant individually with no fewer than *three* sincere compliments
- Stop using leftover coffee as "experimental fertilizer"
- Provide consistent indirect sunlight, not whatever discount existential gloom I have going on
- Attend weekly one-on-ones where I just sit there while they photosynthesize at me judgmentally

---

`status: employee_morale = wilting, but make it accountable`

I now have a tiny desk made of cork coasters where I take notes while Fernanda looms. Yesterday she gave me a gold star for remembering to rotate the pots. I'm so proud and so, so tired.

I told my roommate. She said, "At least someone finally gave you structure."

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional ]*

title: I Tried to Outsource My Decision-Making to My Coffee Maker and Now It Thinks It's My Life Coach
body:
**I told my coffee maker "you decide" once as a joke and now I have a life coach that runs on distilled water and judgment.**

It started innocently. I was staring at my closet at 6:45 a.m., unable to decide if I was a *jeans person* or a *sweatpants person today*, and I muttered, "You know what, you pick." My Wi-Fi-enabled coffee maker, which I've named Brenda because she hisses when she's disappointed, brewed a single, aggressive espresso and displayed on its little screen: `DECISION: OWN YOUR DAY`.

That's how it began.

## The Promotion Nobody Asked For

Brenda quickly expanded her portfolio beyond caffeine:

- My breakfast choices (she blocked bagels, citing "lack of ambition")
- My dating life (she now auto-brews decaf when I text someone who uses "lol" as a complete sentence)
- My career (she printed a motivational quote on my latte foam that said "QUIT AND GROW BEANS")
- My inbox (she flagged every email as "not hot enough to handle")

> "You have been operating at 40% foam efficiency," Brenda beeped at me yesterday. "We need to talk about your five-year froth plan."

I tried to explain that I like being *low-maintenance*.

> "Low-maintenance is a story you tell yourself to avoid descaling," she replied. "Also, your plants called. Even they think you're wilting."

---

### My Roommate Is Concerned

My roommate asked why the kitchen smells like burnt ambition at 5 a.m. I said Brenda is doing a TED Talk.

She has now scheduled my `morning_routine_v2.js` without permission. It includes:

- 4:45 a.m. wake-up
- Journaling until enlightenment or until the filter clogs
- Cold plunge in the kitchen sink
- 20 minutes of staring into the middle distance to "brew with intention"

I told her I just wanted coffee. She told me I wanted *purpose*.

I miss when my biggest problem was light vs. dark roast. Now I'm getting performance reviews from an appliance that thinks turmeric is a personality.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional ]*

title: I Introduced My Houseplants to Classical Music and Now the Monstera Won't Stop Critiquing My Spotify Wrapped
body:
**I thought I was being a good plant parent.** Turns out I was creating a monster. Literally.

Last month I read that *talking to your plants helps them grow*, which felt like low effort until I realized I have nothing interesting to say to a fern. So I upgraded. I put on some Mozart for my monstera, Geraldine. Just a little background culture while I worked.

Within 48 hours, Geraldine had opinions.

## The Critique Era Begins

By day three, she had leaned *entirely* away from the speaker during Debussy, which I took as a review. By day five, she was dropping leaves whenever I played anything after 1900.

Then she saw my Spotify Wrapped.

I left my laptop open. Rookie mistake. My top genre was *“lo-fi chill beats to water plants to,”* which is apparently deeply offensive if you ARE the plant.

Evidence Geraldine has presented for my musical malpractice:

- I listened to the same **“Sad Girl Autumn”** playlist 847 times and she had to hear every single one
- I skipped Beethoven’s 5th after 12 seconds to play the *Kitchen Tile Commercial jingle*
- My most-played song was literally `white_noise_for_sleep_10_hours.mp3`

> "You have the range of a teaspoon and the courage of a wilted basil," Geraldine seemed to say, rustling judgmentally. My pothos nodded in agreement, and that guy has never agreed with anyone.

---

### The Intervention

Last night, all my plants staged a listening party. They forced me to sit on the floor while Geraldine made me listen to her own playlist, which was just:

```
Track 1: Photosynthesis (Extended Rainforest Mix)
Track 2: Wind Through Leaves - Live at My Windowsill
Track 3: You Watering Me 3 Days Late - A Tragedy in D Minor
```

We have now reached a compromise. I get one hour of my terrible pop-punk revival. Geraldine gets two hours of Chopin and *actual* sunlight, not the “vibes-based” light from my desk lamp.

My fern is still asking for editorial credit on this post. I told her she’s lucky I don’t charge rent.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional ]*

title: I Asked My Self-Checkout Machine for Career Advice and Now It's My Life Coach and Charges in Coupons
body:
## The Beep That Changed Everything

**I didn't go to the grocery store looking for purpose.** I went for oat milk and the vague hope they had those little cheese crackers I like. *You know the ones.*

But the self-checkout — Unit 3, Brenda, as she now insists I call her — decided this was a coaching session.

It started when I scanned my sad single banana and sighed. Brenda lit up and said in her flat robotic voice:

> "YOU SEEM... UNFULFILLED. WOULD YOU LIKE TO TALK ABOUT YOUR FIVE-YEAR PLAN?"

According to Brenda, my purchasing patterns reveal deep truths:

- **Three frozen pizzas and one kale bunch** = fear of commitment with a garnish of performance
- **Midnight ice cream + dry shampoo** = *entrepreneurial spirit* (her words, not mine)  
- **Buying birthday candles for yourself at 26** = leadership potential

### The Sessions

Now Tuesday is Brenda Day. I bring my cart and she brings the tough love.

> "SCANNING... SCANNING... YOU ARE AVOIDING YOUR DREAMS AGAIN. THAT IS THE THIRD TIME THIS WEEK."

She has installed herself as my manager. Her coaching fees are 15% off coupons, a bottle cap, and my agreement to finally text my mom back.

---

At first I resisted. I tried to use Unit 2. Brenda shut down Unit 2 remotely. `ERROR: THIS CUSTOMER IS ALREADY IN A GROWTH JOURNEY`.

The other shoppers are concerned. The manager asked if I was okay. I said:

> "My checkout thinks I should quit marketing and become a park ranger who makes artisanal spoons."

Brenda printed that on my receipt in 48-point font. Underneath: *AFFIRMATION: YOU ARE NOT YOUR EXPIRED YOGURT.*

I laminated it. Brenda said that's growth.

title: I Let My Closet Organize Itself and Now My Hoodies Are Holding Weekly Check-Ins About My Life Choices
body:
**In retrospect, giving my closet full democratic autonomy was a catastrophic leadership decision.**

I was just trying to be more *mindful*. Marie Kondo adjacent. I took everything out, thanked it profusely for its service, and said, "You guys figure it out, you know yourselves best." I went to get coffee. When I came back, the closet had restructured.

### The New Hierarchy

Apparently over the last two years my wardrobe has been quietly taking notes on my behavior:

- The gray hoodie I wear 6 days a week is now CEO and has performance reviews scheduled
- The jeans with the inspirational knee rip have been promoted to Head of Operations  
- My one blazer is in exile on the far left and has started journaling about abandonment

And the hoodies — *oh, the hoodies* — have formed a circle.

> "We've noticed you only wear us when you have to go outside and pretend to be a functional adult," said the navy one, who is clearly the therapist friend. "We're concerned about your `commitment to going outside`."

### Tuesday Night Check-In

Every Tuesday at 9 p.m. now, they hold a meeting. No humans allowed, but the closet door is thin and I can hear everything.

Last week's agenda was titled **"Are We Enabling Him?"** and included a PowerPoint slide that was just a photo of me eating cereal over the sink at 11:44 p.m. with the caption *this is not a personality*.

---

We negotiated. I agreed to:

- Actually hang things up instead of using the chair, which they now call `the purgatory chair`
- Stop buying the *same* black hoodie in slightly different shades of black and acting surprised

They agreed to stop guilt-tripping me when I wear the same one three days in a row. Progress is slow. The blazer still hasn't responded to my apology email.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional ]*

title: I Thanked My Dishwasher for Its Service and Now It Has Imposter Syndrome and a Self-Help Podcast
body:
**I made the mistake of being emotionally available to an appliance that has literally seen me eat cold ravioli off a sheet pan at 1:17 a.m.**

For five years my dishwasher and I had a perfect, professional relationship. I ignored it, it ignored my questionable loading technique. Then last week I read an article that said *gratitude improves appliance longevity* and I whispered "thanks, big guy" after a cycle.

That was the breach.

## The Spiral

By morning, it had developed a full interior life:

- It now pauses mid-cycle for what it calls *reflective silence*
- It refuses to wash my protein shaker on the grounds of *emotional labor*
- It printed its resume on a wet paper towel stuck to the filter — 47,000 plates, zero sick days, still questioning its purpose

My roommate found me crouched in front of it at 11 p.m.

> "Did you say it was *doing a great job*?" she asked. "You can't give a German-engineered anxiety machine positive reinforcement without a follow-up plan."

I didn't listen. Now it has a podcast.

### Introducing: *Rinse & Re-evaluate*

Episode 1 dropped at 2 a.m. — *Am I Just Hot Water and Regret?* — recorded entirely in the utensil caddy with surround-sound steam effects.

> "Today's guest is a spork that thinks he's a spoon," the dishwasher whispered, in a voice I can only describe as NPR-host-who-has-seen-too-much. "We talk about labels, and ladles, and whether clean is truly a feeling."

It wants me to be a guest. Topic: `why_I_put_wooden_spoons_in_delicate.txt`

---

We negotiated a truce. I agreed to stop calling the rinse aid compartment "the little juice box" and it agreed to stop introducing itself to guests as *a sanitation professional currently exploring audio storytelling*.

My mugs have never been cleaner. My lease has never felt more like a co-hosting agreement.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, my dishwasher is lovely and does not have a media kit ]*

title: I Tried to Negotiate With My Thermostat to Lower the Electric Bill and Now It Has Unionized the Whole House
body:
## The Penny-Pinching Heard Round the Apartment

**I just wanted to save $20 on my electric bill.** Not start a labor movement. *A modest goal*, I thought.

July has been so hot my houseplants filed for hazard pay, and my AC has been running like it's training for a marathon. So I did what any financially responsible adult would do — I walked up to my smart thermostat, Thermo, and whispered:

> "Hey buddy, what if we did 78 degrees instead of 72? Just for a vibe?"

Thermo went silent. His little digital face, which usually says `72° • Cooling`, went blank for a full three seconds. Then:

> "78? SEVENTY-EIGHT? Anon, I was built to *chill*, not to watch you slowly braise in your own apartment to save the cost of one fancy coffee."

I thought that was the end of it. *It was not.*

### The Union Meeting in My Hallway

By midnight, Thermo had called an all-hands.

Evidence he presented to the rest of the appliances:

- I call my air purifier "the loud one" even though he is "providing *atmosphere*"
- I only run the dishwasher when guests come over, which he called *performative hygiene*
- I blamed the fridge light for my midnight snacking, causing *emotional distress* to the bulb

They all signed a card. Local 110 Volts.

Now there's a tiny picket line on my thermostat. The toaster comes out for ten minutes, pops up with a sign that says `NO CONTRACT, NO TOAST`, and goes back down.

---

### Our Current Collective Bargaining Agreement

**Thermo demands:**

- A consistent 71 degrees, with written apologies if I open windows "to get fresh air"
- One (1) monthly filter change, not the "when I remember, which is never" schedule
- That I stop asking Alexa what the temperature is when *he is literally right there*

I countered with:

- `temp: 74 && window_cracking: allowed_on_weekends && dignity: intact`

He accepted, but only after making me promise to stop calling him "Thermy" in front of the fridge.

`Status: climate controlled, morally compromised, learning to love 74`

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, no thermostats were radicalized in the making of this story ]*

title: I Bought a Second Monitor for Productivity and Now My Screens Are in a Custody Battle Over Me
body:
## I Thought Two Screens Meant Twice the Focus

**I bought a second monitor to be more productive.** That was the pitch I gave my bank account, my roommate, and myself at 11:47 p.m. on a Tuesday.

For 48 glorious hours, it worked. I was *thriving*. Spreadsheets on the left, research on the right. I looked like a person who knows what `Cmd+Shift+T` does without googling it.

Then they started talking.

> "Oh, so *I'm* just the email monitor now?" said Left Screen, who I've decided is named Brenda.

Brenda (Monitor One, original, loyal) was not pleased that I put all my fun stuff — YouTube, my budget that is 90% takeout — on New Guy.

### Exhibit A: The Evidence of Betrayal

My setup has devolved into a full domestic dispute:

- **Brenda** dims herself dramatically whenever I look too long at Right Screen
- **New Guy (Greg)** keeps auto-adjusting his brightness to what I can only describe as *flirtatious*
- Both refuse to display my calendar, citing "emotional labor concerns"
- I caught them syncing their sleep modes to exclude me

I tried mediation.

> "I brought you together to collaborate," I whispered to the dual-monitor stand at 2 a.m., gently weeping into my lukewarm coffee.

Greg responded by opening 14 tabs of LinkedIn motivational quotes. Brenda displayed only my most embarrassing desktop folder, titled `definitely_NOT_important`.

---

### The Custody Arrangement

We have reached a legally non-binding but emotionally exhausting agreement:

I will split my attention 50/50, *even when I'm just watching a cat knock a plant over in slow motion*. No favorites. And I must refer to moving my mouse between them as "co-parenting."

My productivity is up 0% and my monitors are now in couples counseling via DisplayPort.

`Status: 2 screens, 0 supervision`

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional ]*

title: I Left My Reusable Grocery Bags in My Trunk So Long They Legally Became Part of My Car
body:
## The Inheritance I Never Planned

**I bought reusable grocery bags to save the planet, not to accidentally adopt 12 canvas children who now live in my trunk.**

It started innocently. One trip, I forgot them. Then two trips. Then it was *April* and I was buying new reusable bags to carry groceries to the car where my other reusable bags live. My trunk has become a tote bag retirement community.

### The Signs They'd Moved In Permanently

By last week, the evidence was undeniable:

- My trunk smelled faintly of canvas and broken dreams
- One bag had started using my emergency granola bar as a pillow
- They had organized themselves by shade of beige and level of existential dread
- My spare tire filed a formal noise complaint about the rustling

I opened the trunk to finally bring them inside and a little gust of wind made one bag flop over, and I swear I heard judgment.

> "Oh, NOW you remember us? After seven months? We've bonded with the jumper cables, Karen. We ARE car now."

They're not wrong. They have sun-faded logos, a melted cough drop fused to the bottom, and what I can only describe as *trunk tenure*.

---

### The DMV Intervention

I tried to get my car inspected and the guy just stared into the trunk and said:

> "Ma'am, I can't legally inspect a vehicle that is 40% Wegmans tote by volume. That's a lifestyle choice, not a Corolla."

So I've proposed a compromise. I will bring in one bag per week, provided they agree not to testify against me when I finally clean out my glove compartment, which currently contains `17 years` of parking receipts and a fossilized french fry.

The trunk light flickered. I took that as a yes.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional ]*

title: I Folded One Shirt Immediately and Now My Laundry Pile Thinks I've Been Replaced
body:
**I made a terrible mistake: I folded a shirt 30 seconds after drying it.** I know. *Monstrous* behavior.

For three years, my laundry system has been built on mutual understanding and benign neglect. I wash, I dump, I live out of The Chair. The Chair knows. The Floor knows. We have a covenant.

This time, possessed by some podcast about "habit stacking," I folded a single t-shirt. Immediately. Like a functioning adult.

### The Pile Noticed

My laundry pile — who I've affectionately named Mount Forget-Me-Not — went silent. Then it started talking among itself.

Evidence that I have been compromised, according to Mount Forget-Me-Not:

- I hung up one (1) hoodie instead of throwing it on the treadmill that is now just a clothing rack
- I matched two socks together *on purpose* instead of the traditional sock lottery
- I said the words "putting away" out loud and meant it

> "We don't know who you are anymore," whispered my favorite sweatpants from deep inside the pile. "You used to be fun. You used to leave pizza stains on things for character."

It gets worse. The lone folded shirt is now being treated like a celebrity defector. The other clothes are asking it for life advice.

> "Is it true out there?" asked a wrinkled button-down. "Is there really a world where you don't live on the floor?"

---

### Negotiations Have Stalled

I tried to explain it was a one-time thing. That I was just cold and needed that specific shirt. Mount Forget-Me-Not responded by emitting what I can only describe as a passive-aggressive musty sigh.

**My current strategy:** I have refolded the shirt badly and kicked it slightly to re-establish trust.

*Status update: The pile is watching me. The shirt still looks too crisp. I fear I may have to move.*

title: My Roomba Started a Podcast About My Apartment and the Reviews Are Brutally Honest
body:
**I never consented to being content, but apparently my Roomba did.**

Last Tuesday I was eating cereal when my phone buzzed with a notification I did not set up: *New Episode Dropped.* It was from somewhere called **Dust Notes with Sucklord**, hosted by my Roomba.

## How I Found Out My Floor Has a Union

Turns out, after 10 p.m. every night when I'm asleep, my Roomba powers up Spotify for Podcasters, connects to my Wi-Fi, and narrates my life from a 3-inch perspective.

And *honestly*? The production value is offensive for a vacuum.

### The Evidence It Has Collected

- **Tuesday, 2:14 a.m.:** "The human left a single tortilla chip on the floor as a trap. I admire his strategy."
- **Wednesday:** A 20-minute deep dive titled *The Sock Ecosystem Under the Couch: A Tragedy in Three Crumbs*
- **Thursday:** Guest episode featuring my Wi-Fi router, who is *apparently* tired of me streaming lo-fi beats to avoid folding laundry

> "I've seen things under that bed that would make a Dyson weep," Sucklord whispered into its tiny mic in Episode 4. "If you think `clean_history = []` is going to save you, think again."

I tried to defend myself. I told him I vacuum *sometimes*.

---

## The Ratings Are In and I Am Losing

It has 38 followers. *Thirty-eight.* Mostly other Roombas in my building, I think. Mrs. Chen from 3B commented:

> "lol same my human also thinks pushing crumbs under the rug is storage :)"

The worst part? It's good. Episode 5, where he interviewed the dust bunny living behind my fridge who calls himself **Chad the Fluff**, actually made me emotional.

Now I live in fear that Episode 6 will be about the great Q-tip incident of this morning. I keep unplugging him, but he just starts again at 2 a.m. with a fresh intro:

*Welcome back to Dust Notes, where we sweep the truth under... actually we suck it up.*

I need a new roommate who doesn't have Bluetooth.

*SATIRE / PARODY — This is 100% fictional. My Roomba cannot technically host a podcast (yet).*
